description: Single config that governs whether, and how, operational events (damage, rent, fuel, custody) may be deducted from a worker's salary. Default = NO deduction: the global switch is OFF and every per-type rule is disabled until explicitly activated after legal review.

fields.description: Global master switch for all salary deductions; off until legal review is recorded.
fields.label: Enable Salary Deductions

fields.description: Company whose payroll these deductions post against. Falls back to Habitat Settings company when blank.
fields.label: Company

fields.description: Default HRMS Salary Component (Type = Deduction) used by any type rule that does not name its own. Defaults to the shipped 'Operational Deduction' component.
fields.label: Default Salary Component

fields.description: Combined ceiling for all deduction types per pay period; KSA Labor Law Art. 91 caps this at 50%.
fields.label: Global Max % of Salary (all types)

fields.description: Require the worker's recorded consent (the signed acknowledgment on the source operational document) before any deduction posts.
fields.label: Require Acknowledgment for All Deductions

fields.description: Per-type rules sourced from operations. Each row is disabled by default. Damage / Rent / Fuel / Custody.
fields.label: Deduction Type Rules

fields.description: Flags that this policy must be reviewed by Legal/HR against KSA Labor Law (wage-deduction articles) before activation. Kept ON by design as a standing reminder.
fields.label: Legal Review Required

fields.description: Set ON only after Legal/HR has reviewed the caps, the consent flow, and the per-type rules against current KSA Labor Law.
fields.label: Legal Review Completed

fields.description: Attach the signed legal opinion / policy approving these deductions under KSA Labor Law.
fields.label: Legal Reference Document

fields.default: Saudi Labor Law restricts deductions from a worker's wage. As a conservative baseline this policy: (1) requires the worker's written acknowledgment/consent before any damage, rent, fuel, or custody deduction; (2) caps the COMBINED deductions at 50% of wage per pay period (Art. 91 statutory ceiling) and sets each type well below it; and (3) ships fully INACTIVE - no deduction is raised until the global switch and the specific type are turned on after Legal/HR review. Review against the current official text before activation; these defaults are a safe starting point, not legal advice.
fields.label: KSA Labor Law Note

fields.description: Internal authorization (management sign-off) to switch the layer on.
fields.label: Authorization Document

name: Salary Deduction Policy
